q-551.name: Question 1
q-551.worked_solution:
To find the value of $\text{i}$ raised to some positive integer power $n$, we divide $n$ by $4,$ and raise $\text{i}$ to the remainder.

In our case, we have $n=24.$ Dividing the power by $4,$ we get

$$
24÷4=6\,\text{R}0.
$$

So the remainder is $0.$ Therefore,

$$
{\text{i}}^{24}={\text{i}}^{0}=1.
$$

$$
ab={\text{i}}^{2}\cdot {\text{i}}^{9}={\text{i}}^{2+9}={\text{i}}^{11}.

To find the value of $\text{i}$ raised to some positive integer power $n$, we divide $n$ by $4,$ and raise $\text{i}$ to the remainder.

q-86688.name: Question 5
q-86688.worked_solution:
First, using the laws of exponents, we can write

$$
{\text{i}}^{-1}=\frac{1}{\text{i}}.
$$

Multiplying the numerator and denominator by $\text{i},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\text{i}}=\frac{1}{\text{i}}\cdot \frac{\text{i}}{\text{i}}=\frac{\text{i}}{{\text{i}}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We now recall that ${\text{i}}^{2}=-1.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{\text{i}}{{\text{i}}^{2}}=\frac{\text{i}}{(-1)}=-\text{i}.
$$
